articles.headline: Dollar-funding warning shifts to the calendar as plumbing outruns price signals
articles.dek: Seiche’s board reads STRAIN, but the case is prospective rather than a live cash squeeze: dated reserve pressure leads while SOFR remains below IORB.
articles.body_markdown:
The material change is the widening gap between plumbing and market pricing. The Tell is +44.1 percentile points: plumbing is at the 58th percentile and market stress at the 14th percentile, as of 2026-08-28.

That places Seiche’s composite at 45.1, or STRAIN. The claim is deliberately narrow. Known calendar pressure may reduce apparent reserve capacity before secured overnight pricing confirms scarcity. The dated reserve path contributes 11.0 points to the composite, its largest contribution. Overnight cash pricing still signals abundance.

## The mechanism or historical setup

The proposed channel runs from scheduled cash movements and reserve balances through balance-sheet intermediation into secured overnight pricing and facility demand, and then into broader market liquidity. The reserve-demand measure says reserves are below its fitted kink as of 2026-08-26, with an R-squared of 0.62. That is a structural sensitivity measure, not a precise scarcity threshold or proof of a current shortage.

The calendar provides the forcing: month-end, a $137B auction settlement on 2026-09-03, and a corporate-tax date on 2026-09-15 while reserves sit below the estimated kink. The weather component is saturated.

The closest historical comparison is the March 2020 dash-for-cash. The engine’s comparison is context, not a forecast or a publication-vintage backtest. The bounded lesson is that funding monitors can show whether pressure is propagating through intermediation; they cannot establish that an outside shock will occur.

## Quantified evidence with as-of context

Reserves fell $10.4B on the week to $2,925B as of 2026-08-26. The ledger records a $17.9B release from the foreign RRP pool, $14.9B absorbed by the residual, and a $14.8B balance-sheet contraction. Six legs sum to the reserve change, but $22.9B of the balance sheet, or 0.34% of assets, remains in the unnamed residual. That unresolved residual limits a definitive explanation of the movement.

Foreign official activity does not establish an official-sector exit. Over 13 weeks, foreign officials reduced Fed custody Treasuries by $64.4B while foreign RRP parking rose by $56.4B. Seiche characterizes this as a parking rotation, with an official-sector footprint of $2,971B.

The forward path is the concern, rather than an observed spot print. Seiche’s worst-case reserve path reaches $2,893.5B at month-end, $2,883.6B around the 2026-09-03 settlement, and $2,844.8B on 2026-09-15. These are Seiche scenarios, not observed reserves and not forecasts of a market outcome.

The pooled five-business-day event read is 6.2%. It does not turn the calendar into a near-term prediction: its own model evidence says probability levels do not beat climatology and should be used for ranking and alerting rather than as literal odds.

## The strongest counter-case

The counter-case can defeat the thesis. SOFR was 0.9bp below IORB as of 2026-08-26, an abundance signal rather than a scarcity print. Standing Repo Facility take-up was $0.00B as of 2026-08-31, so the backstop was not being tested in size.

Broader market evidence is also calm. Market stress was at the 14th percentile of its own history as of 2026-08-28. The month-end next-turn measure was severity 1, on a scale from 1 calm to 5 extreme, and published its naive 2.5bp estimate rather than its 10.4bp model estimate.

This is not merely a caveat. If the dated drains pass without sustained deterioration in SOFR relative to IORB, material facility demand, or a rise in market stress, the reserve-kink estimate is not identifying a binding constraint in current conditions. Banks may have more usable balance-sheet capacity than the structural signal implies. In that event, the STRAIN label is a failed warning, not an early success.

The $137B settlement on 2026-09-03 is the first observable test. The calendar-led thesis loses force if that settlement and the subsequent 2026-09-15 pressure date pass while SOFR remains below or around IORB, Standing Repo Facility take-up remains at $0.00B, and market stress remains low.

The thesis gains credibility only if dated pressure is accompanied by confirmation in actual plumbing: a sustained adverse move in SOFR relative to IORB, meaningful backstop use, or a marked deterioration from the current low-stress market reading. A lower scenario reserve balance alone does not confirm a realized funding constraint.

## Follow the pressure chain

The chain begins with reserve balances and scheduled settlements. It becomes a funding-capacity problem only if it passes through intermediary balance sheets into secured overnight pricing and facility demand, then reaches wider market liquidity.

That chain currently breaks at confirmation. Reserve and calendar evidence create the warning; SOFR, facility use, and market stress have not transmitted it. The present conclusion is conditional: the system appears more exposed to known dates than the quiet cash tape implies, but dollar funding is not shown to be tight today.

The September 2025 squeeze combined a tax-date drain with Treasury settlement pressure. The historical episode therefore supplies a disciplined sequence to observe: identify the scheduled drain, watch whether secured funding shifts relative to its policy anchor, and then examine whether the standing backstop is used.

The desk guide calls the episode smaller than September 2019, but treats it as a cleaner modern test of the same mechanism. That is the appropriate use of the replay: a calendar event is a pre-registered test, not an alarm.

The episode is the December 2025 year-end squeeze, when Standing Repo Facility use reached a $74.6B record. Its lesson is narrower than a prediction. Funding can tighten through a loss of private intermediation capacity before an overnight benchmark alone provides an unambiguous scarcity signal.

The mechanism is a capacity chain. If marginal balance-sheet deployment becomes less attractive, dealers and banks may intermediate less financing demand. The private channel that redistributes cash, collateral and secured funding narrows. Demand that private balance sheets do not absorb can then appear at the public backstop.

That does not mean aggregate cash is necessarily scarce. It means the ability and willingness to place balance sheets between cash and collateral can be the binding constraint. The counter-case can defeat a claim of present funding tightness: this is a calendar-and-model watch without confirmation in the cash market.

articles.dek: The dash for cash showed how an external shock can turn demand for dollars into a balance-sheet and market-liquidity problem. Today’s tape did not clear the full-story gate.
articles.body_markdown:
This is a historical replay, not breaking news and **not a forecast**. The selected episode is the March 2020 dash-for-cash, dated 2020-03-16. Its construction comparison shows a similarity reading of 0.68 and a 21-business-day lead. Similarity does not establish recurrence.

Today’s tape did not clear the full-story gate. There was no fresh measured change, and auction collection faults reduced the evidence set. This is therefore a desk brief and a watch condition, not a declaration that a funding event is under way.

## The mechanism or historical setup

The March 2020 shock began outside money markets. The lesson is not that a funding monitor predicted its origin. It is that a scramble for dollars and sales of normally liquid securities pushed funding plumbing into the centre of the event: Treasury-market depth deteriorated, cash became the asset everyone wanted at once, and official facilities replaced private intermediation at extraordinary scale.

That sequence identifies the mechanism worth monitoring. An external shock can create simultaneous demand for cash, sales of liquid assets and pressure on the private balance sheets that finance collateral and absorb risk. The resulting problem is not defined solely by an overnight rate. It is a propagation problem: whether stress is moving from a shock into balance-sheet capacity and market liquidity.

The historical lesson has a hard boundary. Funding monitors are strongest on propagation, not omniscience. They may not predict an external shock, but they can show whether it is becoming a balance-sheet and market-liquidity problem.

## Quantified evidence with as-of context

Seiche’s composite was 47 out of 100, labelled STRAIN, on 2026-08-17. It is a Seiche derivation rather than an observed market price. Coverage was 94%, with auctions dead after collection faults; confidence is low before the index is interpreted.

The dominant contribution was the dated reserve path, which added 11.7 points and was saturated. For 2026-08-31, the path estimated reserves at $2,948.5B, with a worst case of $2,849.6B. Further pressure dates were identified for 2026-09-15 and 2026-09-16, with worst-case reserve levels of $2,831.1B and $2,804.1B. These are reserve-path scenarios, not observed reserve prints.

The observed ledger through 2026-08-12 showed reserves down $49.3B on the week to $2,944B. The TGA rebuilt $56.6B and foreign RRP absorbed $39.7B, while the residual released $36.5B. The six legs summed to the reserve change to the dollar, although $18.9B, or 0.28% of assets, remained in the unnamed residual.

Foreign officials cut Fed custody Treasuries by $90.2B over 13 weeks while foreign RRP parking rose $34.8B. The combined official footprint nevertheless fell $55.5B to $2,954B. Seiche calculates that 62% of the custody decline left the official sector rather than rotating within it.

The reserve-demand estimate put reserves $759B below a fitted kink, with an R-squared of 0.62, as of 2026-08-12. Plumbing stood at the 64th percentile of its own history while market stress stood at the 27th, a +37.3 percentile-point Tell. That gap is a condition to investigate, not proof that funding is already scarce.

## The strongest counter-case

The counter-case can defeat a tightening thesis because the current price of overnight cash still signals abundance. SOFR was 3.62% on 2026-08-13, and the editorial read placed it 1.7bp below IORB. EFFR was 3.63%, while IORB was 3.65% as of 2026-08-17. A claim of present system-wide dollar scarcity should be difficult to reconcile with cash pricing below the administered rate.

The official backstop also was not being tested in size. Standing Repo Facility accepted take-up was $0.00B on 2026-08-14. Market stress was at the 27th percentile of its own history; VIX was 14.63 and high-yield option-adjusted spreads were 2.71% on 2026-08-13.

This is more than a claim that markets are quiet. It names the evidence that would be expected if marginal cash were already scarce: pressure in SOFR relative to IORB and meaningful backstop use. Neither was present in the available readings. The defensible reading is conditional calendar and balance-sheet pressure, not an established system-wide shortage.

## A falsifiable next test

The next observable test is month-end, 2026-08-31. The published naive estimate for the SOFR move is 2.2bp, with a band from -1.7bp to 6.7bp and severity of 1 on the calm-to-extreme scale. The model estimate is 9.3bp, but the published estimate is the naive one.

The reserve-path scenario is not itself confirmation; the observable test is whether the calendar date produces a response in the price of cash or use of the backstop.

Start with the ledger: reserves, TGA and foreign RRP. Then examine whether the official-sector footprint is rotating within the system or leaving it. Separate the fitted reserve-demand kink from the observed price of overnight cash. Finally, test whether calendar dates show up in SOFR relative to IORB and in Standing Repo Facility accepted take-up.

The March 2020 replay explains why this ordering matters. A shock can turn market liquidity, collateral finance and balance-sheet capacity into a feedback loop. Current evidence does not establish that loop. The question is whether dollar-funding capacity can tighten through the calendar and balance-sheet channel before overnight cash prices show scarcity. The April 2025 tariff-shock basis unwind supplies a conditional lesson: when a common exit meets limited dealer intermediation, Treasury selling, basis pressure and balance-sheet demand can become one transmission chain.

## The mechanism or historical setup

The April 2025 tariff-shock basis unwind followed a policy shock that changed risk and volatility faster than leveraged relative-value books could adjust. The desk guide’s lesson is not that a large position alone creates a problem. It is whether many holders need the same exit while dealer balance sheets are absorbing the same volatility shock.

That distinction matters for funding analysis. A position may be financeable in orderly conditions. But if holders try to reduce the same trade as volatility rises, dealers may be asked simultaneously to intermediate Treasury flow and absorb volatility. Financing terms, basis pressure and Treasury selling then become connected rather than separate observations.

The current setup has a different initiating force. It is a dated reserve path, not an observed shock in overnight funding. Reserves fell $49.3B in the week through 2026-08-12 to $2,944B. The new change in the dollar-funding picture is a reserve drain meeting a dated settlement—not a spike in the price of overnight cash.

The thesis is narrow: dollar-funding capacity may be tightening through the timing and location of balances before an aggregate overnight-cash shortage appears in market prices. The evidence does not establish a funding event. Indeed, the current price of overnight cash argues against one.

## The mechanism or historical setup

The weekly reserve ledger shows the immediate path of the drain. The TGA rebuild and increase in foreign RRP parking were partly offset by a $36.5B release from the residual, producing the $49.3B decline in reserves. Six legs sum to the reserve change to the dollar, although $18.9B of the balance sheet, or 0.28% of assets, remains in an unnamed residual. The combined official footprint nevertheless fell $55.5B to $2,954B. Seiche calculates that 62% of the custody decline left the official sector rather than moving within it. That is evidence of a smaller official footprint, not proof of a funding shortage.

The mechanism becomes relevant at settlement. Seiche’s reserve-path model places reserves below its estimated demand-curve kink as the $266B settlement arrives. Its central path for 2026-08-20 is $2,935.2B, while its lower error-band outcome is $2,882.1B. The STRAIN label is a Seiche derivation, not an observed market price. The board has full input coverage, but its largest contribution comes from the dated reserve path rather than a live funding-rate dislocation.

The reserve-demand model estimates a kink at $3,703.1B as of 2026-08-12, putting reserves $759B below that estimate. Its fit has an R-squared of 0.62. The strongest counter-case is that funding capacity is not currently tight where a binding constraint should first appear: in the price of overnight cash and use of the official backstop.

Follow the sequence rather than a single print: TGA rebuilding and foreign RRP parking remove or redirect balances; lower reserves meet settlement needs; banks and dealers decide whether to deploy balance sheets; secured rates and official-facility use reveal whether that deployment has become costly.
